$comment: Living policies (standing backlog 8, D-551): one entry per NDIS watch item applied to fixed text, a brief or the standards data. The register marks an adopted document 'review needed' when it was drafted before appliedOn, is in scope, and does not yet carry newSentence; oldSentence is the exact text replaced (null when a sentence was added). The NDIS watch appends an entry whenever it applies an item; src/lib/registers/living-policies.test.ts checks every scope against the catalogue.

changes.newSentence: We tell the Commission about changes and events in its approved form as soon as we know they will happen.
changes.why: Provider Registration Rules s 13A (in force 1 July 2026): notify the Commission of events and changes in the approved form as soon as you know they will happen.

changes.newSentence: If the Commission requires us to take actions on a complaint, we do them, record them in the complaints register and tell the Commission when they are done.
changes.why: Complaints Rules amended 27 January 2026 (F2026L00044): the Commissioner may require the provider to take actions on a complaint (s 16) and complainants are told what was required (s 23B).

changes.newSentence: We do not offer or accept any payment, gift or benefit to attract or keep a participant, or in return for a referral.
changes.why: The Commission's media release on the Securing the NDIS for Future Generations Act 2026 names kickbacks and inducements as a new offence (no section number or start date is stated until the Act's text is read).

changes.oldSentence: Incident and complaint records | [Provider to confirm]
changes.newSentence: Reportable incident records | 7 years from the date we notified the Commission (Incident Rules s 25)
changes.why: Incident Management and Reportable Incidents Rules 2018 s 25: keep the record of a reportable incident for seven years from the notification. (The generator exam, 14 Oct 2026, found that this row sits in a fixed extra the tailored retention schedule does not render; open for the PO, exam Q04.)

changes.newSentence: We check this register each month and start each renewal at least 90 days before the clearance expires. If a clearance expires, the worker stops risk-assessed work that day until a new clearance is issued.
changes.why: The Commission's worker screening renewal-cycle FAQ (January 2026): clearances last up to five years, renewals are accepted up to 90 days before expiry, and an expired worker must be removed from risk-assessed roles immediately.

changes.newSentence: If we use a computer program, including an AI tool, to make or help make a decision that could significantly affect a person, this policy says what personal information it uses and what kinds of decisions it is used for.
changes.why: Australian Privacy Principles 1.7 to 1.9 (Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024) apply from 10 December 2026: a privacy policy must say what personal information an automated program uses and what decisions it makes or helps make.

changes.newSentence: Each participant's support plan carries a medical emergency list with the agreed action for each item.
changes.why: Sector practice from the auditors' webinar: the auditor asks for the participant's medical emergency list and the agreed action; the step names the role that acts and the record it writes to.

changes.newSentence: Complaint records | 7 years from the day the record is made | Complaints Rules s 10(3), read 15 October 2026
changes.why: Batch 45 item 18: the retention schedule is a fixed, sourced table; Complaints Rules s 10(3) (compilation F2026C00165) sets 7 years from the day the record is made; Incident Rules s 12(2) sets what is recorded, not how long; Worker Screening Rules ss 20 and 21 set 7 years for the worker lists.

changes.oldSentence: The Commission, for an unauthorised restrictive practice that caused no harm
changes.newSentence: The Commission, for an unauthorised restrictive practice that is not also one of the kinds above
changes.why: Batch 45 item 19: the escalation table's two Commission rows say what the Incident Rules ss 20 and 21 say; the 24-hour row now names the case where the use of a restrictive practice also caused serious injury or is itself abuse or neglect.

changes.oldSentence: The owner reports the use to the Commission as an unauthorised restrictive practice: within 5 business days, or within 24 hours if the person was harmed (the escalation table in our incident management policy holds the rule).
changes.newSentence: The owner reports the use to the Commission as an unauthorised restrictive practice: within 5 business days; within 24 hours if the use of a restrictive practice also caused serious injury or is itself abuse or neglect (Incident Rules ss 20 and 21; the escalation table in our incident management policy holds the rule).
changes.why: Batch 45 item 19: the 24-hour window is s 20's, which applies when the event is also death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful contact or sexual misconduct; an unauthorised restrictive practice on its own is s 21's 5 business days.

changes.newSentence: A worker whose clearance is pending does not work unsupervised; a worker who is excluded or barred does not work with participants at all.
changes.why: Batch 45 item 24: Worker Screening Rules s 14(1)(a)(ii) (supervised by a person with a clearance while the application is pending) and s 15(2)(a) and (e) (an exclusion or an interim bar means the person is not in the process of obtaining a clearance, so s 13 applies: no risk-assessed role).

Batch 45 item 22: the register's columns match the app (kind, check number, issued, expiry, next check); Worker Screening Rules s 18(3)(d) require the provider's list to hold the application number and the check number, so the app gains the optional field.

changes.newSentence: We tell the Commission, in its approved form, about a change to our contact details, our area, our locations or a significant change in participant or worker numbers (Rules s 13), and about an event that affects our ability to meet a condition of registration, access to our supports, our financial capacity, our organisation or governance, including a change of ownership, or the suitability of the business or its key personnel (Rules s 13A).
changes.why: Batch 45 item 23: the Provider Registration and Practice Standards Rules ss 13 and 13A (compilation F2026C00527) list the changes and events and set 'as soon as practicable' and 'the earlier of' timing; the section also carries one cooperation sentence.
